# Belinda

## Overview

- **Age:** Fourteen years old  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P46](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0046), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- **Role:** Domestic handmaiden and servant for Miss Rosalind Penrose  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043)</sub>
- **Titles:** Belinda the Fourth  <sub>[v2 c21 P46](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0046), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Appearance

She wears notable blue bows in her attire. She continuously practices walking, chin movements, and facial expressions in the mirror to try to copy Nell's graceful demeanor. Her appearance resembles her older sisters who previously served Miss Rosalind.

_Sources: [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048)_

## Personality

Belinda the Fourth is a matter-of-fact, practical, and highly dedicated young girl. She does not mock or express disapproval of Miss Rosalind's imaginative play, unlike some of her sisters. She holds a deep affection and protective concern for her mistress, though she admits to having little patience for men and prone to occasionally breaking dishes.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044), [v2 c28 P53](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0053), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)_

## Traits

- Matter-of-fact  <sub>[v2 c28 P53](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0053)</sub>
- Loyal and caring  <sub>[v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
- Clumsy with crockery  <sub>[v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
- Dislike for men  <sub>[v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>

## Abilities

- Baking and tea preparation  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c21 P61](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0061)</sub>
- Blowing tin horn to produce echoes  <sub>[v2 c21 P71](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0071)</sub>

## Goals

- To emulate Nell's graceful carriage and social demeanor  <sub>[v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039)</sub>
- To move to Boston when she reaches sixteen  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
- To ensure Miss Rosalind is well cared for before she leaves  <sub>[v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>

## History

Belinda the Fourth entered the service of Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage in exchange for room, board, and clothing, following in the footsteps of her elder sisters Belinda, Julietta, and Evelina. She embraced her role without complaining about Miss Rosalind's penchant for pretend tea parties and imaginative games. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke visited Echo Cottage, Belinda served warm biscuits, blew a tin horn, and laughed aloud to demonstrate the forest echoes for them. Over time, she developed a deep admiration for Nell, attempting to practice walking and speaking like her in her mirror, and joined Nell on trips to gather wild strawberries. Noticing Miss Rosalind's failing health and loneliness, Belinda shared her concerns with Nell. Later, when Nell engaged in a secret plan to bring Stephen Stanhope to visit Miss Rosalind, Belinda confronted Nell to ask about the mystery, expressing her earnest hope that Stephen would marry Miss Rosalind so her mistress would not be left alone once Belinda moved to Boston.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P61](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0061), [v2 c21 P71](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0071), [v2 c21 P73](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0073), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P36](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0036), [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044), [v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)_

## Background by volume

- Actual name is Leonora Bowman  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Youngest daughter of Mrs. Bowman  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Succeeded her three older sisters as Miss Rosalind's live-in handmaiden  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> However, I would prefer looking like you to being attractive,  <sub>[v2 c27 P40](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0040)</sub>

> Please, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, it can easily be noticed that a secret exists between you and Miss Rosalind, and I believe, asking for your forgiveness if I am being overly bold, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, that withholding it from me is truly unkind, considering how close we have all been as friends.  <sub>[v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048)</sub>

> Oh, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, what does that mean in plain language?  <sub>[v2 c28 P50](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0050)</sub>

> It’s my hope he weds Miss Rosalind. Certain women are meant to be spinsters right from the beginning, and I fear I belong to that group, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, on account of having precious little tolerance for men. Miss Rosalind, however, never was meant for that. I’ve been dreadfully anxious, pondering whatever would become of her once I grew so large that I must depart for Boston. No other girls remain in our family, and heaven only knows what would happen to her if she hired a stranger who could mock her imaginative play, leave items scattered out of place, and refuse to accept the name Belinda the Fifth. She could find a person who wouldn’t prove as unfortunate as I am at smashing crockery, but she’ll never find a single person who’d cherish her more.  <sub>[v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
